# Read-Back: Colony PCR Screen with a Diagnostic Gel

One person is screening eight candidate bacterial or plasmid clones to identify which ones carry a desired insert. The work starts with thawing reagents and assembling a master mix for PCR, then distributing it into eight reaction tubes with colony suspensions. These tubes are cycled in a thermocycler for 1 hour 50 minutes while, in parallel, an agarose gel is prepared (agarose weighed and microwaved, cooled, poured with stain and comb, then allowed to set). After cycling finishes, the PCR products are spun down and mixed with loading dye. Simultaneously, a DNA ladder is thawed and prepared. Once the gel has set and been transferred to the running rig, all wells are loaded with PCR product and ladder. The gel runs for 40 minutes under voltage, then is imaged on a transilluminator and results recorded. The constraint is that every piece of equipment exists in single-copy: one thermocycler, one microcentrifuge, one microwave, one gel rig, and one transilluminator, all run by one operator. A critical timing detail: the gel can be cast and set *during* the PCR run, so agarose preparation starts 25 minutes into cycling. Loading cannot begin until both the gel is set in the rig *and* the ladder is thawed and ready. The work has no stated deadline and should finish as early as the constraints allow.
